result.title: ReActWAM: Action-Consistent Caching for Efficient World-Action Models
result.summary: World-action models (WAMs) often generate future visual states alongside robot actions, introducing substantial computational overhead during inference. During closed-loop execution, consecutive inference cycles often predict similar action sequences, leading to redundant computation. However, reducing this redundancy requires distinguishing consistent actions from changes that demand fresh computation. To address these challenges, we propose ReActWAM, a training-free framework that combines action-intent-guided prefix skipping with inner-chunk prediction reuse. A coarse-to-fine assessment evaluates motion changes, visual consistency, and action prediction conflicts. For eligible chunks, we draw on first-step differences to adapt the cached latent and network features to the current condition, providing an estimate at a later denoising step that bypasses the redundant prefix. Subsequent inference refines this estimate while reusing stable denoising predictions within the chunk. Experiments across LingBot-VA, FastWAM and the Cosmos family on LIBERO-Long and RoboTwin 2.0 demonstrate $1.41\times$--$5.44\times$ GPU inference speedup, with minimal degradation in task success rates. Real-world experiments on a Franka Research 3 (FR3) robot further achieve $1.46\times$ end-to-end speedup while maintaining success rate.

AI.brief_summary: 提出免训练加速框架 ReActWAM：用动作意图引导的前缀跳过与 chunk 内预测复用，并通过运动变化、视觉一致性和动作冲突的粗到细评估决定是否复用，配合首步差分自适应缓存 latent 与网络特征；在多个 world-action 模型与机器人基准上取得 1.41–5.44 倍推理加速而成功率基本不变。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「判断内部状态可否复用、何时必须重算」的缓存更新与计算跳过机制，可能为 LVR 中跨推理步 latent 复用、动态计算与成本控制的线索，可供核查这些判据是否真正依赖视觉证据。
